summary:
The non-legacy classifier labelled 91.6% of dev LongMemEval user turns TEMPORARY (working tier, expires after 1 hour), so 115 of the 136 answer-bearing user turns were thrown away. The fix has three parts.
(1) Questions and hedges that contain first-person information become EPISODIC instead of TEMPORARY. This applies to user-role turns only.
(2) The final fallback does the same for first-person user text.
(3) A new phatic() early exit keeps pure greetings, thanks, acknowledgements and "say that again" requests in TEMPORARY.
On the lifecycle side, user-role EPISODIC short_term memories now expire after archive_age_days (90) instead of 14 days. Every other short-term memory keeps 14 days, and assistant turns behave exactly as before.
Dev results: memory_retention 21.3% -> 91.0%, mean visible_fraction 17.5% -> 54.9%.
Held-out, run once after freezing: retention 21.0% -> 90.4%, visible_fraction 18.3% -> 55.3%.
The 60 held-out classification cases improve slightly (category 50.0% -> 53.3%, tier 55.0% -> 56.7%) and none got worse.
Legacy classifier, legacy features, ML features, ML scores and tiers are byte-identical across 20,660 inputs. All 162 existing tests pass without edits, and 6 new tests were added.
root_cause:
Two mechanisms caused the loss. Measured on dev, 92 examples, 941 user turns, 136 gold user turns.
(a) main/domain/classification.py returns TEMPORARY as soon as text_rules.uncertain() fires. uncertain() fires on any '?', any quote, or any of if/whether/maybe/might/could/said/asked/not sure. LongMemEval users state their circumstances inside requests, e.g. "I'm planning a trip to the Eastern Sierra and was wondering if you could recommend...", or "ways to keep my living room dust-free, especially with a cat that sheds?".
Rule trace over dev user turns: 743 hit the '?' branch (89 of them gold) and 71 the hedge branch (21 gold). Another 48 reached the final `return TEMPORARY` fallback (5 gold), e.g. "I'm pretty sure I got something for my coworker's baby shower...".
uncertain() exists so that questions do not become asserted facts (claims, reconciliation). Using it as a retention gate is the bug.
(b) TEMPORARY forces the WORKING tier, which expires after 1 hour. In the baseline, 113 of the 116 lost gold user turns were "user:working:expired".
Once (a) is fixed, the binding constraint is the 14-day short_term expiry: 33 of 136 gold user turns are still lost, all as "user:short_term:expired". The dev gap between evidence session and question has median 4 days, p80 17 days and p90 42 days.
The working threshold (0.25) is not a cause. After the fix, the smallest importance score among the 811 user EPISODIC turns is 0.288, and no gold turn is lost from the working tier.

proposed_changes.description:
Add two predicates.
phatic(text): true when the whole message is made of greetings, thanks, acknowledgements, laughter, closings, never-mind, or repair requests ('can you say that again').
self_disclosure(text): true when the speaker says something about themselves (I/we as subject, or my/our + noun). It first removes quoted speech, interrogative inversion ('can I', 'do I'), requests addressed to the assistant ('tell me', 'I was wondering', 'I'd like to know'), reactions ('I see', 'I think', 'I like that') and the roman numeral in 'World War I'.
proposed_changes.unified_diff:
--- a/main/domain/text_rules.py
+++ b/main/domain/text_rules.py
@@ -76,3 +76,55 @@
         r"^(?:i am|i'm)\s+(?:responsible for|working on|part of|based in)\s+\S|"
         r"^(?:we|our (?:team|project|company))\s+(?:use|uses|work|works|is|are|has|have)\s+\S|"
         r"^(?:the|this|that)\s+[\w -]{2,50}\s+(?:uses|requires|belongs to|depends on|is owned by)\s+\S", text)
+
+
+_PHATIC = (
+    r"hi|hello|hey|hiya|yo|howdy|good (?:morning|afternoon|evening|night)|"
+    r"thanks?(?: (?:a lot|so much))?|thank you(?: (?:so much|very much))?|thx|ty|cheers|"
+    r"much appreciated|(?:i )?appreciate (?:it|that)|you'?re welcome|"
+    r"ok(?:ay)?|k+|sure|yes|yeah|yep|yup|no|nope|nah|alright|all right|fine|cool|great|nice|perfect|awesome|wow|"
+    r"got it|gotcha|understood|noted|will do|sounds (?:good|great)|(?:that )?makes sense|fair enough|"
+    r"i see|i agree|i understand|i (?:get|got) it|i know|no idea|i have no idea|i (?:don't|do not) know|"
+    r"(?:i'?ll|i will)(?: (?:try|do) (?:that|it|this))?|(?:i )?(?:have|gotta|got) to go|"
+    r"(?:i'?m|i am) (?:good|fine|ok|okay|great|back|done|here|ready|sorry|glad|confused|lost|not sure)|"
+    r"lol|lmao|rofl|ha(?:ha)+|hehe|"
+    r"bye|goodbye|see you(?: later)?|see ya|talk (?:to you )?later|ttyl|"
+    r"never ?mind|nvm|forget (?:it|about it)|no worries|no problem|np|my bad|"
+    r"sorry|pardon(?: me)?|huh|what|come again|excuse me|please|"
+    r"(?:(?:can|could|would) you (?:please )?)?(?:say|repeat) (?:that|it)|"
+    r"that'?s (?:great|good|cool|helpful|perfect|awesome|fine|ok|okay|interesting|it)|"
+    r"now|then|again|anyway|so|really|too|for (?:now|today)"
+)
+# First person that carries no information about the user: interrogative inversion,
+# requests addressed to the assistant, and reactions to what the assistant said.
+_NON_DISCLOSING = (
+    r"\b(?:can|could|would|will|should|shall|may|might|must|do|does|did|am|are|have|has|was|were) (?:i|we)\b|"
+    r"\b(?:tell|show|give|help|let|send|remind) (?:me|us)\b|"
+    r"\b(?:i|we) (?:was|were|am|'m|are|'re) (?:just )?(?:wondering|curious)\b|"
+    r"\b(?:i|we)(?:'d| would) (?:really )?(?:like|love|appreciate)"
+    r"(?: it if| (?:you|your help|some help)| to (?:know|learn|ask|hear|understand|find out))\b|"
+    r"\b(?:i|we) (?:want|wanted|need|needed) to (?:know|ask|learn|understand|find out)\b|"
+    r"\b(?:i|we) (?:really )?(?:love|like) (?:it|that|this|these|those|them|the idea|your)\b|"
+    r"\b(?:i|we) (?:didn't|did not|don't|do not) (?:catch|get|follow|hear|understand)\b|"
+    r"\b(?:i|we) (?:get|got) it\b|"
+    r"\b(?:i|we) (?:see|agree|understand|guess|mean|think|suppose|hope|know|wonder|wondered|believe|appreciate)\b|"
+    r"\bworld war i\b"
+)
+
+
+def phatic(text: str) -> bool:
+    """Greetings, thanks, acknowledgements and repair requests with nothing else in them."""
+    words = ' '.join(re.sub(r"[^\w\s']", ' ', normalize(text)).split())
+    return not words or re.fullmatch(rf"(?:(?:{_PHATIC})(?: |$))+", words + ' ') is not None
+
+
+def self_disclosure(text: str) -> bool:
+    """The speaker states something about themselves (circumstances, plans, possessions,
+    events), possibly inside a question or a request. Quoted speech is somebody else's."""
+    text = normalize(text)
+    if phatic(text):
+        return False
+    if not text.startswith(('"', "'")):
+        text = re.sub(r'"[^"\n]*"', ' ', text)
+    text = re.sub(_NON_DISCLOSING, ' ', text)
+    return matches(r"\b(?:i|we)\b|\b(?:my|our)\s+\w", text)

proposed_changes.description:
Non-legacy path only. Three changes:
(S0) Phatic messages return TEMPORARY right after the task_action check.
(S1) In the uncertain() branch, return EPISODIC instead of TEMPORARY when a user-role input self-discloses. The input is recorded as an observation and never as a claim: the question and hedge gates for claims and reconciliation are unchanged.
(S2) The final fallback returns EPISODIC for self-disclosing user text.
The role check keeps assistant turns unchanged, since first person in an assistant turn describes the assistant. The legacy=True path never reaches the new code.

proposed_changes.description: (L) User-role EPISODIC memories in the short_term tier expire after archive_age_days (90). This reuses the existing staleness constant rather than adding a new tuned number. Every other short_term memory keeps 14 days: tasks without a due date, assistant episodic turns, and refreshed facts. Working and long_term are unchanged.

proposed_changes.description:
New regression tests, 6 tests and 24 subtests. They cover:
- first person inside questions and hedges -> EPISODIC, short_term, 90-day expiry, no claim
- plain first-person statements -> EPISODIC
- phatic and generic messages -> TEMPORARY and working, including 'Can you say that again?', 'I see.', 'never mind', 'World War I'
- reported speech and assistant first person are not user disclosures
- other short-term memories keep the 14-day window
- the legacy classifier ignores the new rules
The full file is in the scratch copy at the path below.
proposed_changes.unified_diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_user_disclosure_retention.py
@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+"""Developer-authored regression cases for keeping what users say about themselves."""
+import unittest
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+
+from main import MemoryCore, MemoryInput
+from main.domain.classification import MemoryClassifier
+from main.domain.text_rules import phatic, self_disclosure
+
+NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 12, 9, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+
+
+def process(text, role='user'):
+    return MemoryCore().process(MemoryInput(text, 'u', 's', role=role, timestamp=NOW))
+
+
+class UserDisclosureRetentionTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_first_person_content_inside_questions_and_hedges_is_kept(self):
+        for text in ["I'm planning a trip to Lisbon in May, can you suggest neighbourhoods?",
+                     'I have a golden retriever who hates baths, any tips?',
+                     'Do you know if I need a visa to visit Japan?',
+                     'What are some ways to keep my living room dust-free?',
+                     "I'm not sure if my mom would like a Kindle for her birthday.",
+                     'I was thinking about selling my guitar collection, maybe online?']:
+            with self.subTest(text=text):
+                record = process(text)
+                self.assertEqual(record.category.value, 'episodic')
+                self.assertEqual(record.tier.value, 'short_term')
+                self.assertEqual(record.expires_at, NOW + timedelta(days=90))
+                self.assertIsNone(record.claim)  # an observation, never an asserted fact
+
+    def test_plain_first_person_statements_reach_episodic_instead_of_temporary(self):
+        for text in ["I'm vegan.", "I'd like to set up a budget because I'm saving for a house."]:
+            with self.subTest(text=text):
+                self.assertEqual(process(text).category.value, 'episodic')
+
+    def test_phatic_and_generic_messages_stay_working_memory(self):
+        for text in ['Thanks!', 'ok', 'lol', 'Never mind.', 'Can you say that again?', 'I see.',
+                     'I agree', 'Got it, thanks.', "I didn't catch that, can you repeat it?",
+                     'I have no idea', 'Hey, good morning!', 'What is the capital of Australia?',
+                     'Can you tell me more about rate locks?', 'Can I also get a room with a fireplace?',
+                     'I think that is a great idea!', 'Can you summarize the causes of World War I?']:
+            with self.subTest(text=text):
+                record = process(text)
+                self.assertEqual(record.category.value, 'temporary')
+                self.assertEqual(record.tier.value, 'working')
+
+    def test_reported_speech_and_assistant_first_person_are_not_user_disclosures(self):
+        self.assertFalse(self_disclosure('She said "I moved to Berlin".'))
+        self.assertEqual(process('She said "I moved to Berlin".').category.value, 'temporary')
+        reply = "I'd be happy to help! I recommend visiting Alfama, what dates are you considering?"
+        self.assertEqual(process(reply, role='assistant').category.value, 'temporary')
+        self.assertEqual(process(reply, role='assistant').tier.value, 'working')
+
+    def test_other_short_term_memories_keep_two_week_window(self):
+        self.assertEqual(process('Buy groceries').expires_at, NOW + timedelta(days=14))
+        episode = process('I submitted my report today.', role='assistant')
+        self.assertEqual(episode.expires_at, NOW + timedelta(days=14))
+
+    def test_legacy_classifier_ignores_disclosure_rules(self):
+        incoming = MemoryInput('Do you know if I need a permit for the trail?', 'u', 's')
+        self.assertEqual(MemoryClassifier(legacy=True).classify(incoming).value, 'temporary')
+        self.assertEqual(MemoryClassifier().classify(incoming).value, 'episodic')
+        self.assertTrue(phatic('Thanks, that makes sense.'))
+        self.assertFalse(phatic('Thanks, I moved to Pune last week.'))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

tests:
Patched scratch copy: cd $S/repo && $PY -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider gives 168 passed and 136 subtests passed (162 existing plus 6 new).
- No existing test was changed. Every assertion in test_memory_core, test_conversational_rules, test_conversation_task_extensions, test_memory_lifecycle_updates, test_memory_reconciliation, test_quality_improvements and test_cleanup still holds. That includes 'Buy groceries' expiring at +14 days, 'She said "..."' being temporary, and hedged or question statements ('I might live in Mumbai.', 'Do I live in Mumbai?') never producing a claim or superseding a fact.
- None of these existing tests encodes the bug, so none needs to change.
- tests/test_ml_importance.py: 4 of 4 pass. tests/test_neural_importance.py: 4 of 4 pass. Nothing was skipped.
- Legacy byte-for-byte check: cd $S/{base,repo} && PYTHONPATH=. $PY $S/scripts/legacy_check.py --output $S/out/legacy_{base,patched}.jsonl. It covers 20,660 inputs: every LongMemEval oracle turn, all 456 gold benchmark memories and the probes, each as both user and assistant. The SHA-256 hashes are identical between base and patched for the legacy classifier category, FeatureExtractor(legacy=True) features, MLFeatureExtractor features, and the MemoryCore.with_ml() record (category, features, importance_score, tier).
- The only difference in the with_ml pipeline is expires_at on 508 user-role EPISODIC short_term records. This is because LifecycleManager is shared; see risks.
- Pre-existing flaky test: tests/test_conversation_task_extensions.py::TaskWorkflowExtensions::test_cli_occurrence_and_explicit_rescheduling fails intermittently with "Target task not found, inactive, newer than update..." on the UNPATCHED copy too (5 of 40 runs on base, 6 of 40 on patched). It looks like a wall-clock ordering race between consecutive CLI calls, unrelated to this change.
risks:
1. Storage grows, on purpose. Visible fraction roughly triples (18% -> 55% on held-out) and post-cleanup bytes rise about 12%. Almost all of the growth is user turns: on dev, assistant visibility is unchanged at 21.7% and user-turn visibility goes from 9% to 89%. LongMemEval oracle sessions are evidence sessions where nearly every user turn contains first-person content (914 of 941 on dev), so this benchmark cannot show much selectivity among user turns. Selectivity is shown only by the self-authored probes (78/80 phatic and 12/12 generic dropped), which is a weak, non-independent check. In real chat logs with many phatic turns the visible fraction should be lower; this was not measured.
2. self_disclosure is a regex heuristic.
   - It treats any first-person subject or my/our+noun as information. That includes low-value plans like "I think I'll add a few hashtags" and anaphoric remarks.
   - It misses information carried without first person ("Can you make a reservation for me at Roscioli tomorrow at 7?") or behind an inversion ("Can I get a room at The Edgewater?").
   - The 'world war i' special case covers one known ambiguity of the pronoun 'I'; other roman-numeral uses ("Elizabeth I") are not handled.
3. Disclosures are recorded as EPISODIC, not as facts. They are never claim-extracted or reconciled, so a later contradicting statement does not supersede them. Durable facts phrased conversationally ("I'm a nurse on the night shift") are retained for 90 days but not promoted to long_term (see the held-out classification errors).
4. The lifecycle change is shared by every MemoryCore, including with_ml and with_neural. Their legacy preprocessing, features, scores and tiers are byte-identical, but user EPISODIC short_term records now expire after 90 days instead of 14. If that pipeline's lifecycle must also stay frozen, it would need its own LifecycleManager setting.
5. The 90-day horizon reuses archive_age_days. Changing that constant now also changes retention of user events.
6. The S0 phatic early exit also applies to assistant turns and to a few phrases that used to hit other rules, e.g. "I have no idea" (previously SEMANTIC/long_term via the 'i have' pattern). That is intended, but it is a behaviour change outside LongMemEval.
7. Assistant-turn losses (6 dev gold turns, single-session-assistant at about 64-69%) are deliberately left unchanged. Remembering assistant recommendations would be a separate design decision.
8. Latency of the extra regexes was not measured. They are linear-time and run once per message.
